items.title: Remove the fixed-length truncation so late-diverging rejection reasons keep distinct digests
items.context: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:479 truncates the normalized reason to 200 characters before hashing. ProofStory gap lists share a preamble longer than that, so two different gaps hash identically. Hash the full normalized reason, retaining only a large sanity bound to cap CPU on pathological input.
items.userSees: node packages/main/dist/tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.js prints a passing check stating that two real DEV-gate rejection renders differing only past the former 200-character cut produce different digest keys.

happy.desc: gateFailureDigest applied to two reconstructions of the real DEV-gate rejection render (machine.ts:179 preamble plus renderProofStoryDiagnosticReport), identical for their first 244 normalized characters and differing only in the outstanding gap codes, returns two different keys.
The same two rejections routed through bumpGateFailureCount leave maxGateFailureCount at 1, so assessBreaker does not trip, which is the actual operator-visible consequence.

edge.desc: A rejection reason far longer than any realistic gate message still produces a digest, and the retained sanity bound is exercised rather than silently absent.
Two reasons that are identical up to the sanity bound and differ only beyond it are documented as collapsing, so the bound's residual behavior is stated rather than assumed away.

adversarial.desc: Restoring only the fixed-length truncation makes the new smoke assertions fail, proving the check is bound to this change and not to some unrelated property.

verificationEvidence.note: NOT DELIVERED AS ORIGINALLY WRITTEN, recorded as such. The C1 class was fixed on main by story B-cc54, which keeps the 200-character prefix and folds structurally-extracted gap-id signals into the hash basis; this branch adopted main's version and does not change the truncation. What this story delivers of the item is bounded and named: 'must-differ signal-less-long-rejection [guard: signals-conditional-prefix]' — when a rejection yields no signals the prefix widens, so a late-diverging reason keeps a distinct key. Recorded by case name and guard tag with no hand-written totals: every earlier re-recording drifted because it counted, and the partial re-recording before this one left sibling notes contradicting their own item (F-045/F-046/F-047). This set was written whole, against the matrix as the suite prints it.

'must-differ signal-less-long-rejection [guard: signals-conditional-prefix]' drives the real bumpGateFailureCount and asserts the counter consequence, not the hash alone. Mutation M10 (prefix cut made unconditional) fails exactly that case. Recorded by case name and guard tag with no hand-written totals: every earlier re-recording drifted because it counted, and the partial re-recording before this one left sibling notes contradicting their own item (F-045/F-046/F-047). This set was written whole, against the matrix as the suite prints it.

Case 'must-still-collapse scope-extension-proposal-ordinal-past-window [guard: prefix-window-residual]' pins the accepted residual: when two rejections carry identical signal sets and differ only in a substantive ordinal past the prefix window, they still collapse — verified never worse than main, which collapses that pair too. Mutations M12 (window 200 to 600) and M12b (200 to 592) each fail exactly that case and each leave B-cc54's suite green; the window stays at 200 for byte-compatibility with B-cc54, not because no relaxation exists. An earlier note claimed widening was unavailable; that absolute was measured false and is withdrawn.

The same residual from the opposite side: the within-window pair is asserted DISTINCT by 'must-differ scope-extension-proposal-ordinal [guard: substantive-id-whole-token]'. The fixture precondition prints the measured divergence positions for both directions, so the bound is pinned rather than described.

Case 'must-differ proofstory-gap-signal-set [guard: signals-fold]' is this story's guard against silently regressing B-cc54's mechanism: two rejections with identical 200-character prefixes but different non-empty signal sets must digest differently. Mutation M11 (basis collapsed to prefix alone) fails exactly that case. The earlier claim that 'bcc54-cross-vendor-noise' served this purpose was FALSE and is retracted — that case passes under M11, which the test-coverage lane proved. Case names and guard tags only, deliberately no counts: every prior re-recording of this evidence went stale because it hand-wrote totals that the next fix round changed (F-013, F-017, F-028, F-039, F-040 were all that defect).

items.title: Narrow the path normalizer to machine-specific absolute roots only
items.context: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:475 rewrites any slash-bearing token, collapsing DEV/REVIEW with DEV/TEST and src/core/alpha.ts with src/core/beta.ts. Restrict it to absolute paths anchored at machine-specific roots so relative repo paths and slash-bearing identifiers stay distinct while host-varying paths still collapse.
items.userSees: The convergence-breaker smoke prints passing checks stating that DEV/REVIEW and DEV/TEST digest differently, that two files under a shared first path segment digest differently, and that the same lock path under /Users and under /private/var still digests identically.

happy.desc: Two rejection reasons differing only in a slash-bearing identifier (the phase pair DEV/REVIEW versus DEV/TEST) produce different digest keys.
Two rejection reasons naming different repo-relative files under a shared first segment (src/core/alpha.ts versus src/core/beta.ts) produce different digest keys.

edge.desc: The same logical lock path rendered under a machine-specific root (/Users/... versus /private/var/...) still produces one digest key, so host-varying paths keep collapsing.
A path that begins at a machine-specific root but continues into repo-relative segments is normalized once, without leaving a partially-rewritten remainder that could differ per host.

adversarial.desc: Restoring the greedy slash-anchored regex makes the new distinctness checks fail while the machine-path collapse check keeps passing, proving both directions are independently bound to this change.

verificationEvidence.note: Case 'must-differ phase-pair [guard: path-rule-overreach]' asserts DEV/REVIEW and DEV/TEST digest differently, printing both compared values literally. Case names and guard tags only, deliberately no counts: every prior re-recording of this evidence went stale because it hand-wrote totals that the next fix round changed (F-013, F-017, F-028, F-039, F-040 were all that defect).

Case 'must-differ in-repo-file-path [guard: path-rule-overreach]' asserts two files under a shared first segment digest differently. Case names and guard tags only, deliberately no counts: every prior re-recording of this evidence went stale because it hand-wrote totals that the next fix round changed (F-013, F-017, F-028, F-039, F-040 were all that defect).

Cases 'must-still-collapse machine-absolute-path' and 'delimiter-attached-absolute-path' [guard: path-rule-collapse] assert host-varying absolute paths, including those introduced by a colon, equals or comma, still share one key and still trip the breaker. Case names and guard tags only, deliberately no counts: every prior re-recording of this evidence went stale because it hand-wrote totals that the next fix round changed (F-013, F-017, F-028, F-039, F-040 were all that defect).

Case 'must-still-collapse machine-path-into-repo-relative-segments [guard: path-rule-collapse]' asserts a path continuing from a machine root into repo-relative segments is consumed in one match, leaving no per-host remainder. Case names and guard tags only, deliberately no counts: every prior re-recording of this evidence went stale because it hand-wrote totals that the next fix round changed (F-013, F-017, F-028, F-039, F-040 were all that defect).

Two revert-proofs, one per direction. Mutation M1 (path rule widened to main's form) fails the path-rule-overreach cases plus, by a real cross-dependency, 'signal-less-long-rejection' and 'init-check-issue-ordinal-past-window'. Mutation M2 (path rule deleted) fails the path-rule-collapse cases plus 'bcc54-cross-vendor-noise'. Subsets are named in the suite output rather than counted here. Case names and guard tags only, deliberately no counts: every prior re-recording of this evidence went stale because it hand-wrote totals that the next fix round changed (F-013, F-017, F-028, F-039, F-040 were all that defect).

items.title: Narrow the numeric normalizer to standalone numbers only
items.context: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:476 rewrites digit runs inside identifier tokens, collapsing CHK-001 with CHK-002. Restrict it so digits attached to an identifier survive while free-standing counters such as attempt numbers still collapse.
items.userSees: The convergence-breaker smoke prints a passing check stating that a rejection naming CHK-001 and one naming CHK-002 digest differently, alongside a passing check that two attempts differing only in a free-standing counter still digest identically.

happy.desc: Two rejection reasons differing only in an identifier-embedded ordinal (CHK-001 versus CHK-002) produce different digest keys.

edge.desc: Two rejection reasons differing only in free-standing counters and an ISO timestamp still produce one digest key, so genuine retries of one failure keep accumulating.
A story id such as B-bf52, whose digits are attached to an identifier, survives normalization, so rejections naming different stories are not conflated.

adversarial.desc: Restoring the unconditional digit-run rewrite makes the identifier-ordinal distinctness check fail while the free-standing-counter collapse check keeps passing.

verificationEvidence.note: Cases 'must-differ checklist-ordinal', 'finding-ordinal', 'unfixed-bug-ordinal' and 'init-check-issue-ordinal' [guard: substantive-id-allowlist] assert that an ordinal naming WHICH lifecycle artifact failed survives normalization, printing both compared values literally. Case names and guard tags only, deliberately no counts: every prior re-recording of this evidence went stale because it hand-wrote totals that the next fix round changed (F-013, F-017, F-028, F-039, F-040 were all that defect).

Case 'must-still-collapse bare-attempt-ordinal [guard: digit-rule-collapse]' asserts two attempts differing only in a free-standing counter still share one key and still trip the breaker, matching the frozen userSees. 'lease-heartbeat-age' and 'lane-counts' extend the same direction. Case names and guard tags only, deliberately no counts: every prior re-recording of this evidence went stale because it hand-wrote totals that the next fix round changed (F-013, F-017, F-028, F-039, F-040 were all that defect).

Case 'must-differ scope-extension-proposal-ordinal [guard: substantive-id-whole-token]' asserts a COMPOUND artifact id keeps its trailing ordinal distinct; mutation M6 fails exactly that case. Two cases pin the converse, both guarded review-bookkeeping-not-allowlisted: 'stale-review-run-evidence' and 'review-loop-ordinal', plus 'init-check-issue-ordinal' which MOVED to must-still-collapse after review showed the init-check issue id is reviewer-self-assigned, overwritten wholesale on every init_check_set, and remediated by re-running the reviewer — the same instability that disqualified rr-, rp- and rl-. Case 'must-still-collapse embedded-test-output-hyphen-compounds [guard: substantive-id-token-start]' guards the regression where a hyphen-joined compound such as de-bug-2 survived normalization because a hyphen creates the very word boundary the old guard relied on.

Revert-proofs by named mutation, each re-derived from source with the mutation anchor asserted to apply: M7 (allowlist emptied) fails checklist-ordinal, finding-ordinal, unfixed-bug-ordinal and scope-extension-proposal-ordinal — an earlier note described M7's effect wrongly, because before the empty-allowlist safety the corrupted regex aborted an earlier assertion and named no case at all. M8 (b- added) fails bcc54-story-id-digits here and CHK-002:adversarial:2 in B-cc54's suite. M9 (rr-/rp-/rl- added) fails the review-bookkeeping cases. M14 (i- re-added) fails init-check-issue-ordinal. M15 (token-start guard weakened back to a word boundary) fails embedded-test-output-hyphen-compounds. M13 (numeric placeholder alphabet) fails the same four as M7. M5b (ISO and digit rules both deleted) aborts at a section-7 assertion BEFORE the matrix and names no matrix case — recorded as it actually behaves, not as a named-subset proof.

items.title: Extend the convergence-breaker smoke with a substantive-versus-incidental digest matrix
items.context: packages/main/src/tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.ts:180-182 asserts distinct reasons do not accumulate but uses fixtures too short and too plain to reach any collapse rule. Add the four must-differ cases (long-preamble ProofStory gaps, phase pair, checklist ids, in-repo file paths) and the three must-still-collapse cases (timestamps and attempt counters, machine-specific absolute paths, hex digests), each driving the real bumpGateFailureCount and maxGateFailureCount path so the counter consequence is proven, not just the hash.
items.userSees: npm run test:convergence-breaker exits zero and its output lists the must-differ and must-still-collapse digest cases by name, each reporting the resulting gate-failure counter value rather than only the hash.

happy.desc: Every must-differ case drives the real bumpGateFailureCount path twice and then asserts maxGateFailureCount is 1, proving the counter consequence rather than only the hash inequality.
npm run test:convergence-breaker exits zero from a clean build, so the matrix is reachable through the root full test suite that gates DONE.

edge.desc: Every must-still-collapse case drives bumpGateFailureCount twice and asserts maxGateFailureCount reaches 2 and assessBreaker still trips, proving the breaker keeps catching a genuine repeat.
The pre-existing assertions in this smoke, including the reset-clears-counter case, keep passing unchanged alongside the new matrix.

adversarial.desc: Each of the three normalizer changes reverted individually causes a named subset of the matrix to fail and leaves the rest passing, so the matrix localizes which rule regressed instead of failing as one opaque block.

verificationEvidence.note: Every must-differ case prints keys=2 counter=1 breaker=proceed, each having driven the real bumpGateFailureCount twice and read back maxGateFailureCount and assessBreaker. The suite's closing banner DERIVES its inventory from the case arrays rather than hand-typed totals, so the count cannot drift from the matrix. Case names and guard tags only, deliberately no counts: every prior re-recording of this evidence went stale because it hand-wrote totals that the next fix round changed (F-013, F-017, F-028, F-039, F-040 were all that defect).
Ran from a clean build in the worktree and exited zero, confirming the matrix is reachable through the root npm test chain that lattice.config.json lists as a doneRequiredCommand.

Every must-still-collapse case prints keys=1 counter=2 breaker=trips, proving the brake still catches a genuine repeat. The set covers machine paths, both B-cc54 fixtures, review-bookkeeping ids, the past-window residual, bare attempt ordinals, lease heartbeat ages, lane counts, hex ids and ISO timestamps. Case names and guard tags only, deliberately no counts: every prior re-recording of this evidence went stale because it hand-wrote totals that the next fix round changed (F-013, F-017, F-028, F-039, F-040 were all that defect).

B-cc54's suite is byte-unmodified by this story (git diff main on that path is empty) and exits 0. The completeness guard is now BIDIRECTIONAL: it fails naming an UNCLASSIFIED prefix when a scanned producer has no entry, and naming a NO PRODUCER entry when the allowlist or exclusion list carries a prefix nothing emits — the drift that produced this story's own enumeration errors is now caught by the suite instead of by the next review round. Case names and guard tags only, deliberately no counts: every prior re-recording of this evidence went stale because it hand-wrote totals that the next fix round changed (F-013, F-017, F-028, F-039, F-040 were all that defect).

Revert-proofs cover every changed rule and both guard directions, each named in the suite output: M1/M2 path rule, M3 digit rule, M4 hex rule, M5b ISO-and-digit disjunction, M6 whole-token, M7/M8/M9 allowlist membership, M10 conditional prefix, M11 signals fold, M12 window widening (which also breaks B-cc54, proving widening is unavailable), M13 placeholder encoding, and G1/G2/G3 for the guard's unclassified, no-producer and broken-citation directions. Case names and guard tags only, deliberately no counts: every prior re-recording of this evidence went stale because it hand-wrote totals that the next fix round changed (F-013, F-017, F-028, F-039, F-040 were all that defect).
